You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2023 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 25 [20 marks]: Future Century Gaming Pty Ltd operates an online gaming platform targeting players aged 18−40 in Australia. It has been in operation since 2012, providing subscription access to a variety of online games.
The business is considering expanding into emerging global markets but is finding it challenging to recruit and retain skilled, qualified game designers and developers in Australia. It is considering international labour markets to overcome staff shortages.
The business has decided to finance its expansion into global markets through external sources.
The directors have asked you to write a business report in which you:
• outline some of the challenges including the global factors of costs, skills and supply the business may need to consider in recruiting and retaining staff
• compare the use of debt and equity as sources of finance
• recommend ONE source of finance this business could use to fund its expansion.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Provides a comprehensive outline of the challenges including the global factors of costs, skills and supply in relation to recruiting and retaining staff | Provides a comprehensive comparison of the use of debt and equity finance | Provides a comprehensive recommendation to the business for ONE source of finance to fund the expansion | Makes effective use of the information provided, demonstrating extensive knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Presents a sustained, logical and cohesive business report integrating relevant business terminology and concepts
13–16 marks: Provides a substantial outline of the global factors of costs, skill and supply in relation to recruiting and/or retaining staff | Provides a clear comparison of the use of debt and equity finance | Provides a sound recommendation to the business for ONE source of finance to fund the expansion | Makes sound use of the information provided, demonstrating knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Presents a logical and cohesive business report integrating relevant business terminology and concepts
9–12 marks: Provides a sound outline of the global factors of costs and/or skills and/or supply in relation to recruiting and/or retaining staff | Provides a sound comparison of debt and equity finance | Provides a recommendation to the business for ONE source of finance to fund the expansion | Makes use of the information provided, demonstrating some knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Includes features of a business report and uses some business terminology and concepts
5–8 marks: Provides some outline of global costs and/or skills and/or supply | Makes a statement about debt and/or equity finance | Makes a statement about a possible source of finance | Includes some features of a business report and uses some basic business terminology and/or concepts
1–4 marks: Makes some reference to human resource strategies and/or finance | Uses basic business terminology


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Strategies in human resource management
• Global – costs, skills, supply


WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: provide an outline of the challenges of global costs, skills and supply and effectively relate these challenges to both recruiting and retaining staff
Better responses: make accurate and detailed comparisons between the use of debt and equity
Better responses: identify a specific and appropriate source of finance and provide comprehensive reasons in favour of using this source of finance to fund the business’s expansion
Better responses: structure the response using appropriate business report features and apply relevant terminology and concepts.
To improve: improving the structure of the business report when outlining the challenges of global costs, skills and supply and relating these to retaining staff
To improve: addressing the term ‘compare’, rather than only providing a description or outline or debt and equity finance
To improve: identifying a specific source of finance rather than referring to debt and equity generally
To improve: applying the hypothetical business situation more effectively to the challenges of global costs, skills and supply.

STUDENT RESPONSE:

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
